messages.subject: One Factor CFA Limitations
parts:
The measurement invariance article by Fischer & Karl (2019) states of CFA that: "One of the biggest challenges is that a simple
structure in which items only load on one factor is often
empirically problematic;" yet, no citation is provided. Could someone please provide me with more information as to why a one factor CFA is often empirically problematic. Thank you!

messages.author: 3db1352ea447cb3c
messages.subject: Re: One Factor CFA Limitations
parts:
This is a fact of life. Finding a group of more than three indicators that measure just a single latent construct (and have nothing else in common) is simply a very rare situation. If you want some mathematical elaboration, you may look at Shapiro, A. (1982). Rank-reducibility of a symmetric matrix and sampling theory of minimum trace factor analysis. Psychometrika, 47, 187-199.
Best regards, Gregor

messages.subject: Re: One Factor CFA Limitations
parts: Thank you Gregor for your response! This is interesting because the fit indices seemed almost "too good to be true," with CFIs = 1.00 and RMSEAs = .000 in a variety of samples. In these cases the chi-square values are lower than the degrees of freedom as could be expected. So, I am just not sure whether or not I can trust the results? I will look into the literature that you suggest (thank you!); however, please let me know if you have any further comments given the results I am finding.
